column_semantics: The Schedule of Investments splits interest into separate Ref. Rate, Cash, and PIK columns. For floating-rate debt, the Ref. Rate column gives the base rate abbreviation, the Cash column gives the cash spread/rate, and the PIK column gives the separate paid-in-kind spread/rate on top. Rows with only PIK economics leave Cash blank and put the PIK rate in the PIK column.

rationale: The filing does not present one all-in rate with PIK included. It prints separate interest columns headed Ref. Rate, Cash, and PIK. Named rows with PIK show the cash spread in Cash and the PIK spread in PIK, for example S+ / 2.75% cash / 2.75% PIK for Inovalon and S+ / 2.50% cash / 3.00% PIK for Bayshore. Therefore the stated cash/spread rate excludes PIK; PIK is quoted separately and is additive.
